nordic-atelier.title: Nordic Atelier
nordic-atelier.description: A quiet luxury storefront for a Scandinavian design house — editorial pacing, tactile product storytelling, and checkout that disappears into the experience.
nordic-atelier.longDescription: Nordic Atelier needed a storefront that felt as considered as their furniture. We rebuilt the brand site around editorial storytelling: large material studies, restrained motion, and a checkout flow designed to stay invisible until the moment of purchase. Performance was treated as a design constraint — sub-second LCP on product pages without sacrificing imagery.

pulse-finance.title: Pulse Finance
pulse-finance.description: A dense product surface made elegant. Real-time dashboards with cinematic motion and a design system built for scale.
pulse-finance.longDescription: Pulse Finance launched a Series B product surface that had to communicate trust and technical depth at once. We designed a dark-first system with cinematic motion cues for live data, then engineered a component library that product and marketing teams could both extend. Accessibility and keyboard flows were non-negotiable for a regulated audience.

lumen-studio.title: Lumen Studio
lumen-studio.description: Immersive project archives with scroll-driven spatial storytelling — light, shadow, and material as the narrative.
lumen-studio.longDescription: Lumen Studio’s portfolio had to feel spatial. We built scroll-driven case studies where light and material lead the story, with optional WebGL walkthroughs for flagship projects. A headless CMS lets architects publish new work without breaking the cinematic pacing of the archive.

orbit-labs.title: Orbit Labs
orbit-labs.description: From pitch deck to production in eight weeks. A developer-facing product site that sells through clarity, not noise.
orbit-labs.longDescription: Orbit Labs needed a marketing site that developers would trust. We stripped the noise, built documentation-adjacent product pages, and shipped an edge-deployed Next.js stack in eight weeks. Demo requests more than doubled after launch — driven by clarity, speed, and a product narrative that respected a technical audience.

faq.title: Straight answers
faq.subtitle: The practical details clients ask before we start.
faq.pageDescription: Answers about TavsWebs timelines, budgets, tech stack, brand work, and taking over unfinished website projects.

0.q: How long does a typical project take?
0.a: Most marketing sites land in 6–10 weeks. Product platforms and immersive builds run 10–16 weeks depending on scope and content readiness.

1.q: Do you work with existing brands?
1.a: Yes. We can extend an established identity or rebuild from first principles. Either way, the web experience should feel like a natural evolution — not a costume.

2.a: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, Framer Motion, and React Three Fiber when immersion earns its place. CMS options include Sanity, Contentful, and custom solutions.

3.q: Can you take over an unfinished project?
3.a: Often. We’ll audit the codebase, design debt, and performance baseline before proposing a path forward — sometimes a rebuild is cheaper than a rescue.

4.a: Meaningful custom work typically starts around €8,000. Complex product and 3D experiences scale from there. We’ll be transparent before any kickoff.
